scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The tourdion originated in the Burgundian court in the mid-15th century and became popular throughout France.
Early mentions appear in 'La grant danse macabre' (1499).
It was famously documented by Pierre Attaingnant in 1530 and Thoinot Arbeau in 1589.
on_screen: Map: France · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The tourdion was a social dance used for entertainment and courtship.
Its lively nature provided a rhythmic contrast to more somber dances.
In modern times, it has become associated with drinking songs and historical reenactments.
Today it is a revived tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Danced as a couple, it uses the 'cinq pas' (five steps) over six beats.
It begins in a 'posture' with one foot slightly forward.
The dancer performs four small kicks ('pieds en l'air') with 'petits sauts' (small hops), followed by a 'saut moyen' (medium jump) into a cadence that switches the lead foot.
Watch for Cinq pas, Pied en l'air, Saut moyen.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (P8RlYeu5GBs)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couple dance; moves through the hall, often following a basse danse path.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music is in triple meter (6/8 or 3/4), often featuring a recurring rhythm of a half note followed by a quarter note.
Historical ensembles used flutes and tambourines.
Listen for the Flute, Tambourine, Lute, Harpsichord.
The pulse is 3/4 or 6/8 at about 120 beats a minute.

A driving triple-meter pulse characterized by a 'jumping' rhythm in the accompaniment. The melody is often smooth with small intervals, supported by a rhythmic bass line that mimics a tambourine's strike.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Performed in Renaissance court settings or festive gatherings.
Dancers wore period attire such as doublets and hose for men, and gowns for women.
The setting was typically a ballroom or a festive hall where it followed the basse danse.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Thoinot Arbeau provided the primary technical description in 'Orchésographie'.
Pierre Attaingnant published the first collected music.
In Italy, it was known as the 'tordiglione' or 'dordiglione'.
It is a sibling to the galliard, sharing the same musical structure but differing in elevation.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Tourdion is sibling of Galliard: Shares the same music and five-step structure but uses higher jumps.
Tourdion is parent of Basse danse: The tourdion was traditionally performed as the concluding section of a basse danse suite.
